column2: 动词义最早见于 16 世纪，来源不明；与中古低地德语 pusseln（摆弄、瞎忙）一类词或属同源
column3: a game or question that needs thought to solve, or to confuse someone
column5: The puzzle took her all evening.|His answer puzzled the whole class.
column6: something that holds the mind up until solved – 想不通就卡在那儿的东西
column7: 谜题：需要动脑才解得开的题|使困惑：让人一时想不明白

column2: 法语 pyramide ← 古法语 piramide ← 拉丁语 pyramis ← 希腊语 pyramis；更早或出埃及语 pr-m-ws（塔之高）
column3: a solid shape with a square base and four triangular sides
column5: They climbed the great pyramid at dawn.|Draw a pyramid with a square base.
column6: a stack narrowing to a single point – 层层收窄到一个顶点的堆体
column7: 金字塔：埃及那类巨型石构|棱锥：底为多边形、侧面收于一点的几何体

column2: 中世纪拉丁语 quantifico（定量），由逻辑学家 William Hamilton 引入英语
column3: to measure or express something as an amount
column5: It is hard to quantify the damage.|Researchers quantified the loss in tonnes.
column6: putting a how-much on something – 给某物定出一个多少

column2: 晚期拉丁语 quantitātīvus，由 quantity ＋ -ative 构成
column3: relating to amounts that can be measured
column5: The study used quantitative methods only.|They need quantitative data before deciding.
column6: to do with how much rather than what kind – 关乎多少而非性质
column7: 数量的：与数目大小有关|定量的：靠测得的数值来判断

column2: 中古英语 quantite ← 古法语 quantité ← 拉丁语 quantitās，源自 quantus（多少）
column3: an amount of something that can be counted or measured
column5: We ordered a large quantity of paper.|Quality matters more than quantity here.
column6: the how-much of something – 某物的多少

column2: 中古英语 querele ← 中古法语 querelle ← 拉丁语 querēla（抱怨、控告），源自 querī（抱怨）
column3: an angry argument, or to argue angrily
column5: The brothers quarrelled over the money.|Their quarrel lasted several weeks.
column6: a complaint pushed into open dispute – 抱怨激成公开的争执

column2: 借自德语 Quarz ← 中古高地德语 quarz／twarc，出自西斯拉夫语（比较波兰语 twardy 硬）
column3: a hard glassy mineral found in many rocks
column5: Quartz crystals lined the narrow cave.|The watch uses a quartz movement.
column6: a hard clear mineral grain in rock – 岩石中坚硬透亮的矿粒

column2: 约 1510 年起见于苏格兰语；通常认为出中古低地德语 queer（斜的）或德语 quer（横斜）← 原始日耳曼语 *þwerhaz
column3: strange or different from what is expected
column5: A queer noise came from upstairs.|He had a queer look on his face.
column6: set across the expected line – 与常规走向斜错开的

column2: 中古英语 quenchen ← 古英语 cwenċan ← 原始日耳曼语 *kwankijaną
column3: to put out a fire, or to satisfy thirst
column5: Cold water quenched his thirst quickly.|Rain quenched the last of the flames.
column6: bringing a burning or craving to an end – 让燃烧或渴求就此止住
column7: 解渴：把渴的感觉压下去|熄灭：让火停止燃烧

column2: 中古英语 queue ← 古法语 cöe（尾）← 俗拉丁语 cōda ← 拉丁语 cauda（尾）
column3: a line of people waiting for something
column5: A long queue formed outside the door.|We queued for nearly an hour.
column6: people strung out in a tail – 像尾巴一样拖出的一列人
column7: 队列：依次排开的一条线|排队：加入这条线等候

column2: 中古英语 quiete ← 古法语 quiet ← 拉丁语 quiētus，为 quiēscere（安歇）的过去分词
column3: making little or no noise
column5: The street stays quiet after nine.|She spoke in a quiet voice.
column6: at rest with little sound – 处在少声的安歇状态

column2: 中古英语 quilte ← 古法语 coilte ← 拉丁语 culcita（垫褥）
column3: a warm bed cover made of layers stitched together
column5: She spread a quilt over the bed.|The old quilt kept them warm.
column6: layers stitched into one padded cover – 缝合成一整片的夹层盖被

column2: 中古英语 quiten ← 古法语 quitter ← 拉丁语 quietus（安歇的、免除的）
column3: to stop doing something, or to leave a job or place
column5: He quit smoking three years ago.|She quit the company last spring.
column6: releasing oneself and coming to rest – 撂开手让自己歇下来
column7: 放弃：中途停下不再做|离开：从职位或处所退出

column2: 中古英语 quiver ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 quivre ← 古荷兰语 cocar（箭筒）← 原始西日耳曼语 *kokar（容器）
column3: to shake with small rapid movements, or a case for arrows
column5: Her voice quivered as she spoke.|He pulled an arrow from the quiver.
column6: a small rapid trembling, and the case that holds arrows – 细密的抖动，以及盛箭的筒
column7: 颤抖：细而快地不停抖动|箭袋：背在身上盛箭的筒

column2: 1780 年代起见于记载，来源不明；一说出自方言 whiz 的变体，一说原义为「怪人」
column3: a short test of knowledge, or to question someone
column5: The class took a short quiz today.|Reporters quizzed him about the delay.
column6: a quick round of questions – 一轮快问快答
column7: 测验：小规模的知识检查|问答：连续提问并作答

column2: 拉丁语 quota pars（该占的那一份）中的 quota
column3: a fixed share or limited number allowed
column5: Each region received a fishing quota.|They filled the quota by June.
column6: the share reckoned as one part – 按份额算定的那一份

column2: 中古英语 quoten ← 古法语 coter ← 中世纪拉丁语 quotāre（标号），源自拉丁语 quotus（第几）
column3: to repeat words said or written by someone else
column5: She quoted two lines from the poem.|They quoted a price for the work.
column6: marking out words by number to cite them – 标出号码以便援引
column7: 引用：照原样重述他人的话|报价：给出所要的价钱

column2: 中古英语 rabet ← 盎格鲁拉丁语 rabettus ← 古法语方言 rabotte，或为中古荷兰语 robbe 的指小形，更早词源不明
column3: a small animal with long ears that digs burrows
column5: A rabbit slipped under the wire fence.|Rabbits dug holes across the lawn.
column6: a long-eared burrowing animal – 长耳、会打洞的小动物

column2: 由 race ＋ -ial 构成；race 一支 ← 中古法语 race ← 意大利语 razza
column3: relating to differences between groups of people by descent
column5: The report examined racial differences carefully.|Racial equality remains the stated goal.
column6: to do with descent groups – 与血统群体有关的

column2: 中古英语 radical ← 拉丁语 rādīcālis（属于根的），源自 rādīx（根）
column3: relating to the basic nature of something, or favouring extreme change
column5: The plan needs a radical rethink.|Radical groups rejected the compromise.
column6: reaching down to the root – 一直探到根上的
column7: 根本的：涉及最底层的|激进的：主张彻底改变的

column2: 古英语 reġnboga ← 原始日耳曼语 *regnabugô，由 rain ＋ bow（弧）复合而成
column3: a curved band of colours seen in the sky after rain
column5: A rainbow appeared above the wet field.|Children pointed at the bright rainbow.
column6: a rain-made arch of colour – 雨造出的彩色弧

column2: 由 rare ＋ -ly 构成；rare ← 古法语 rare ← 拉丁语 rārus（稀疏）
column3: not often
column5: He rarely leaves the house now.|Snow rarely falls in this valley.
column6: happening at thin intervals – 出现得稀疏

column2: 古英语 rēdere（读者、占卜者）← 原始西日耳曼语 *rādāri，由 read ＋ -er 构成
column3: a person who reads
column5: The magazine has thousands of readers.|Every reader received the same notice.
column6: the one who takes in written words – 把字读进去的那个人

column2: 中古英语 redily，由 ready ＋ -ly 构成
column3: quickly and without difficulty
column5: The parts are readily available here.|She readily agreed to the change.
column6: in a state already prepared to go – 已经备好随时可动的样子
column7: 容易地：不费力就能做到|乐意地：不推托就答应

column2: 古英语 rǣding（阅读），由 read ＋ -ing 构成
column3: the activity of looking at and understanding written words
column5: Reading before bed helps him sleep.|The meter reading rose again.
column6: taking in what is written – 把写下的东西读进去
column7: 阅读：看并理解文字|读数：仪表上读出的数值

column2: 中古英语 rebellioun ← 古法语 rebellion ← 拉丁语 rebelliō，源自 rebellāre（再兴战）
column3: an organized attempt to remove a government by force
column5: The rebellion spread to three provinces.|Troops crushed the rebellion within days.
column6: taking up arms again against a ruler – 再度对当权者动兵

column2: 由 re-（再）＋ call 构成，或仿拉丁语 revocāre 与法语 rappeler 而造
column3: to remember something, or to order something to be returned
column5: She could not recall his name.|The maker recalled thousands of cars.
column6: calling something back to hand or mind – 把东西或记忆叫回来
column7: 召回：命令已发出的东西返回|回忆：把过去的事叫回脑中

column2: 借自拉丁语 recēns（新近的）
column3: happening or made a short time ago
column5: Recent changes improved the whole service.|His recent letter arrived only yesterday.
column6: only lately come about – 刚不久才发生的

column2: 借自中古法语 récipé ← 拉丁语 recipe（取用吧），为 recipere（取、收）的第二人称单数命令式
column3: a set of instructions for cooking a dish
column5: She followed the recipe exactly this time.|The recipe needs four large eggs.
column6: an instruction that begins take this much – 以「取多少」开头的一份说明
column7: 食谱：做某道菜的步骤说明|配方：配制某物的成分与比例

column2: 借自中古法语 récipient ← 拉丁语 recipiēns，为 recipere（收受）的现在分词
column3: a person who receives something
column5: Each recipient signed for the parcel.|The recipient of the prize spoke briefly.
column6: the one who takes what is given – 把送来之物接过去的人
column7: 接受者：收下某物的一方|受领人：正式领取的人
